findings.title: Filesystem-equivalent Unicode symlink excludes still permit mirror data loss
findings.evidence: crates/blit-core/src/transfers/filter.rs:565 — paired_name uses Unicode lowercase rather than filesystem equivalence; when pairing fails, stored_name returns None for symlinks at line 535. Reproduced on case-insensitive macOS with src/σ pointing outside the source and absolute exclude src/ς: both paths had the same symlink inode, but local and wire patterns remained ./ς with no warning. Mirror deleted dst/σ/saved.txt and its directory. An NFD-stored café symlink excluded using uppercase NFC CAFÉ behaved identically. Exact stored-spelling controls preserved both destination subtrees.
findings.predicted_failure: A valid absolute exclude naming an existing symlink through another filesystem-equivalent spelling silently fails to protect its destination counterpart; mirror deletes pre-existing data. This leaves cr-g3fix2-1 and cr-g3fix-1 materially open.
findings.better_approach: Recover the entry's stored name using filesystem-aware lookup or candidate identity checked without following symlinks. Cover Unicode case equivalence and normalization with destination-survival tests.

findings.title: Escaped literals also exclude entries named like their encoded pattern
findings.evidence: crates/blit-core/src/transfers/filter.rs:446 — escaped literal components reach ExcludeRules, whose fs_enum.rs:131 fallback also compares the encoded pattern as ordinary text. Reproduced with alias pointing to src/data[1], alongside src/data[[]1[]] and src/data1. Copying with --exclude <alias> omitted both data[1]/private.txt and the unrelated data[[]1[]]/private.txt, while copying data1/private.txt. The generated ./data[[]1[]] matches the intended name through globset and the unrelated encoded name through glob_match.
findings.predicted_failure: Copy or backup silently omits an unrelated subtree whose name equals an escaped pattern's textual representation, despite successful completion.
findings.better_approach: Evaluate escaped patterns consistently as globs; do not additionally interpret their encoded text through the exact/prefix fallback. Add a negative control containing the escaped representation as an actual filename.

findings.title: Windows peers reinterpret escaped Unix backslashes as directory separators
findings.evidence: crates/blit-core/src/transfers/filter.rs:466 — a resolved Unix name back\slash is emitted as ./back[\]slash. On Windows, fs_enum.rs:83 invokes normalize_separators, whose line 147 rewrites this to ./back[/]slash. A temporary test against the actual ExcludeRules::compile branches confirmed that the Unix rule leaves back/slash/saved.txt in scope while the Windows rule excludes it. The remote mirror consumes these rules through transfer_session/mod.rs:4181. This was verified through the parameterized compiler on macOS, not a Windows runtime.
findings.predicted_failure: A Unix-to-Windows mirror excluding an aliased directory containing a literal backslash also excludes the unrelated destination subtree back/slash from deletion, retaining stale files outside the requested exclusion.
findings.better_approach: Preserve a canonical wire-pattern dialect and normalize native separators before escaping, without rewriting escaped literals on the receiving peer. Test Unix-generated wire patterns under both platform rules.
